meta.title: What Type of PM Are You?
meta.description: A 2-minute scenario quiz to discover your PM archetype

intro.subtitle: Not self-scoring — real scenarios, gut reactions. Discover your PM archetype and growth path.

result.ctaTitle: Want a deep AI assessment based on your real experience?
result.ctaDesc: Caliber's full assessment analyzes 16 PM dimensions based on your real work experience, generating a professional report with growth advice and action plans.

craftsperson.name: The Craftsperson
craftsperson.tagline: Relentless pursuer of user experience excellence
strengths: Translates vague requirements into precise product specs
Natural intuition for user experience
Consistently reliable delivery quality
blindSpots: May over-polish details while losing sight of the big picture
Room to improve business acumen
Sometimes struggles to ship 'imperfect' solutions

strategist.name: The Strategist
strategist.tagline: Bridge builder between business and product
strengths: Finds the core leverage point in complex environments
Translates business goals into product roadmaps
Strong cross-functional influence
blindSpots: May overlook execution-level details
Can get caught up in grand narratives
Frontline user pain perception could be deeper

growth-hacker.name: The Growth Hacker
strengths: Spots opportunities others miss through data
Expert at designing and analyzing A/B tests
Superb intuition for conversion funnels
blindSpots: May over-rely on data while missing qualitative insights
Tends to chase short-term metric gains
Limited patience for long-term product experience

visionary.name: The Visionary
strengths: Anticipates tech trends and positions ahead
Excels at 0-to-1 product creation
Inspires teams and stakeholders with vision
blindSpots: May drift from current user needs
Gap between ideals and execution
Sometimes underestimates 'boring but important' foundational work

operator.name: The Operator
operator.tagline: Making complex things happen in order
strengths: Creates order from chaos
Top-tier cross-team coordination and driving ability
Delivers projects on time with high quality
blindSpots: May over-rely on process at the expense of innovation
Tends to fall into firefighting mode
Product intuition and strategic thinking have room to grow

questions.scenario: The CEO suddenly announces: 'We need to cut 50% of the product roadmap.' Your first reaction?
options: Pull up the data immediately — find which features have the lowest retention and ROI, use data to decide what to cut
Map each project's alignment with company strategy — keep what's most critical to the long-term vision
Talk to core users first — find out what they can't live without, decide from the user's perspective
Call a meeting with team leads to align priorities — make sure cuts don't disrupt ongoing critical deliveries

questions.scenario: A competitor just launched a viral AI feature. Everyone's asking 'should we follow?'
options: Study the underlying tech stack first — is there a more cutting-edge approach to leapfrog them?
Pull their user reviews and growth data — analyze if it's actually working for retention and acquisition
Go back to our user scenarios — do users need this specific feature or the underlying need behind it?
Assess our resources and roadmap — can we follow quickly without derailing core deliveries?

questions.scenario: Your product has been live for 3 months but DAU is flat. The boss is getting impatient.
options: Build a complete data funnel — find the biggest drop-off point and design targeted experiments
Step back and ask: are we fighting in the wrong market? Should we redefine the target user?
Interview 20 churned users in depth — find the real reasons they left, fix experience issues one by one
Align marketing, ops, and engineering — create a 30-day sprint plan to break through together

questions.scenario: Engineering says 'technically possible, but at least 3 months.' Your response?
options: Dive into the technical approach with engineers — can we break it into smaller deliverables and ship an MVP first?
Re-evaluate business value — if the market window closes in 3 months, is it still worth building?
Look for shortcuts or third-party solutions — validate the hypothesis with minimum cost first
Evaluate whether we can reallocate resources or reprioritize parallel projects to accelerate

questions.scenario: The company is entering a brand-new market (e.g., expanding overseas). How do you approach it?
options: Research tech trends and user behavior differences in the target market — can new tech create differentiation?
Run a simple landing page + paid ads test to validate market demand with minimum cost
Analyze competitive landscape, regulations, and business models — develop a phased entry strategy
Find benchmark users in the target market, deeply understand their workflows and pain points

questions.scenario: Designer presents a beautiful but complex interaction scheme. How do you decide?
options: Sketch a simplified flow yourself — ensure every step matches user mental models and habits
Run a quick A/B test — compare conversion data between the complex and simplified versions
Judge from positioning — does this complex interaction reinforce our core value proposition?
Pull in design and engineering to discuss — find the optimal trade-off between dev cost, timeline, and UX

questions.scenario: An internal tool is severely slowing down the team, but nobody wants to fix it.
options: Build a prototype over the weekend — prove how much efficiency improves, use facts to drive the decision
Do the math: wasted team labor cost vs. renovation investment — write a business case for leadership
Research automation tools or AI solutions — see if low-code/AI can solve it quickly
Launch a cross-team improvement project — set clear milestones and owners to drive formal delivery

questions.scenario: In a user interview, someone describes a use case you never imagined. It's niche but they're very excited.
options: Dig deeper into the underlying need — could this evolve into the next core feature?
Note it, then check the database for similar behavior patterns — use data to prioritize
Listen carefully, document the full user story — think about how to elegantly support it within existing architecture
Evaluate it against the broader product vision and market positioning — does it open a new market segment?

questions.scenario: Boss wants a new feature in 2 weeks, but you know quality will suffer.
options: Scope down — find the core experience path, do only the critical 20% but make that 20% perfect
Design a minimal experiment — ship a gray-release version in 2 days, let data decide how much more to invest
Show the boss full-version vs. minimal-version ROI comparison — negotiate for reasonable timeline or resources
Create a detailed 2-week sprint plan with daily deliverables — coordinate the team for all-out delivery

questions.scenario: You just took over a product line. Previous PM left zero documentation, codebase is messy. First move?
options: Use the entire product end-to-end — document every UX issue and bug to establish a quality baseline
Pull all user data and business metrics — figure out how much value this product actually creates
Chat with every engineer, designer, and ops person involved — understand history and team dynamics
Research the market and competitors — rethink the strategic positioning and future possibilities

meta.title: 你是哪种PM？

result.ctaDesc: Caliber 完整评估基于你的真实工作经历，通过 AI 分析 16 个 PM 维度，生成专业报告、成长建议和行动计划。

craftsperson.name: 匠心产品人
craftsperson.tagline: 用户体验的极致追求者
strengths: 能把模糊需求转化为精确的产品方案
对用户体验有天然直觉
交付质量稳定可靠
blindSpots: 可能过度打磨细节而忽视大局
商业敏感度有提升空间
有时难以割舍「不完美」的方案

strategist.name: 全局战略家
strategist.tagline: 商业与产品的桥梁建造者
strengths: 能在复杂环境中找到核心杠杆点
将商业目标转化为产品路线图
跨部门影响力强
blindSpots: 可能忽视执行层面的细节
容易被宏大叙事带偏节奏
对一线用户痛点的感知可能不够深

growth-hacker.name: 增长黑客
strengths: 用数据发现别人看不到的机会
擅长设计和分析 A/B 测试
对转化漏斗有超强直觉
blindSpots: 可能过度依赖数据而忽视定性洞察
容易追求短期指标增长
对长期产品体验的耐心有限

visionary.name: 未来洞察者
visionary.tagline: 看到别人看不到的可能性
strengths: 能预判技术趋势并提前布局
擅长从 0 到 1 创造新产品
用愿景激发团队和利益相关者
blindSpots: 可能脱离当前用户的实际需求
理想与执行之间容易出现落差
有时低估「无聊但重要」的基础工作

operator.name: 卓越运营者
operator.tagline: 让复杂的事情有序发生
strengths: 能在混乱中建立秩序和流程
跨团队协调和推动能力一流
让项目按时高质量交付
blindSpots: 可能过于依赖流程而限制创新
容易陷入「救火」模式
产品直觉和战略思维有提升空间

questions.scenario: CEO 突然宣布：「我们要砍掉 50% 的产品路线图。」你的第一反应是？
options: 立刻拉数据，看哪些功能的用户留存和 ROI 最低，用数据说服老板砍哪些
先梳理每个项目和公司战略目标的关联度，保留对长期愿景最关键的项目
找核心用户聊聊，搞清楚他们最离不开的功能是什么，从用户视角决定
召集各团队 lead 开会，对齐优先级，确保砍掉的部分不会打断正在进行的关键交付

questions.scenario: 竞品刚发布了一个火爆的 AI 功能，团队都在问「我们要不要跟？」
options: 先研究这个功能的底层技术路线，思考有没有更前沿的方式弯道超车
拉竞品的用户评价数据，分析他们的获客和留存变化，判断是否真的有效
回到我们的用户场景，想想用户真正需要的是这个功能还是背后的需求
评估我们的资源和路线图，判断在不影响核心交付的前提下能否快速跟进

questions.scenario: 你负责的产品上线三个月了，DAU 一直涨不动，老板开始不耐烦了。你怎么办？
options: 搭建完整的数据漏斗，找到流失最严重的环节，设计针对性的实验来优化
退后一步看看：我们是不是在错误的市场里打仗？是否需要重新定义目标用户
深入访谈 20 个流失用户，找到他们不回来的真正原因，逐一修复体验问题
拉齐市场、运营、研发团队，制定一个 30 天冲刺计划，集中火力突破

questions.scenario: 工程团队说「这个需求技术上可以做，但至少要 3 个月」。你的反应是？
options: 和工程师一起深入技术方案，看能不能拆分成更小的可交付单元，先上 MVP
重新评估这个需求的业务价值——如果 3 个月后市场窗口关闭了还值得做吗？
考虑有没有技术捷径或第三方方案，用最小成本先验证假设
评估是否可以调配更多资源或调整并行项目的优先级来加速交付

questions.scenario: 公司准备进入一个全新市场（比如从国内走向海外），你会怎么切入？
options: 研究目标市场的技术趋势和用户习惯差异，思考能不能用新技术建立差异化优势
先做一个简单的落地页 + 付费广告测试，用最低成本验证市场需求
全面分析目标市场的竞争格局、监管环境和商业模式，制定分阶段进入策略
找到目标市场的标杆用户，深入了解他们的工作流和痛点，打造本地化产品体验

questions.scenario: 设计师拿出了一个方案，视觉上很好看但交互逻辑复杂。你怎么决策？
options: 自己画一个简化的交互方案，确保每一步都符合用户心智模型和使用习惯
做一个快速的 A/B 测试，看用户在复杂方案和简化方案上的转化数据对比
从产品定位角度判断——这个复杂交互是否强化了我们的核心价值主张？
拉上设计和工程一起讨论，在开发成本、上线时间和体验之间找到最优折中

questions.scenario: 公司有一个内部工具严重拖慢了团队效率，但没有人愿意花精力去改。你的选择是？
options: 趁周末自己先做个原型，证明改进后效率能提升多少，用事实推动决策
算一笔经济账：团队因此浪费的人力成本 vs 改造投入，写一份 business case 给管理层
研究市场上的自动化工具或 AI 方案，看能否用低代码/AI 方式快速解决
发起一个跨团队改进项目，设定明确的里程碑和 owner，推动它作为正式项目落地

questions.scenario: 用户访谈中，有个用户提了一个你从没想过的使用场景，看起来很小众但他非常激动。你会？
options: 深入挖掘这个场景背后的需求本质，思考是否能演化成下一个核心功能
先记录下来，然后去数据库里查有多少用户有类似行为，用数据判断优先级
认真倾听并记录完整的用户故事，思考如何在现有产品框架内优雅地支持它
把它放到更大的产品愿景和市场定位中评估，判断它是否打开了新的市场空间

questions.scenario: 老板要求你在两周内上一个新功能，但你知道质量肯定会打折扣。怎么处理？
options: 拆分功能范围，找出核心体验路径，只做最关键的 20%，但确保这 20% 完美
设计一个最小可行实验，用 2 天上线一个灰度版本，根据数据反馈再决定投入多少
向老板展示完整版和极简版的 ROI 对比，争取合理的时间线或资源
制定详细的两周冲刺计划，明确每天的交付物，协调团队全力以赴按时交付

questions.scenario: 你刚接手一个新产品线，发现前任 PM 留下的文档几乎为零，代码库也很混乱。第一步做什么？
options: 先把产品完整地用一遍，记录每一个体验问题和技术 bug，建立质量基线
调取所有用户数据和业务指标，搞清楚这个产品到底为公司创造了多少价值
和所有相关的工程师、设计师、运营人员聊一圈，了解历史背景和团队现状
研究这个产品所在的市场和竞品，重新思考它的战略定位和未来可能性
